The Future

By: Eugene Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
………..the future used to be years away, but now it has arrived.

Unique Selling Point:
Story about massive changes that will very soon affect each and everyone on the planet -- from the child in the slums of Africa and India to the corporate mogul

Summary:
In the past, we thought of the future as, well… the future. We thought of a time, still years away. But that has changed. In the latter half of the 20th century more knowledge was created than in the previous 10 000 years of human existence. In the first 10 years of the 21st Century more knowledge was created that in all of the 20th Century, and it is speeding up exponentially.
And this will, and is, changing our lives and our world profoundly.

Further information:
In the past, we thought of the future as, well… the future. We thought of a time, still years away. But that has changed. In the latter half of the 20th century more knowledge was created than in the previous 10 000 years of human existence. In the first 10 years of the 21st Century more knowledge was created that in all of the 20th Century, and it is speeding up exponentially.

And this will, and is, changing our lives and our world profoundly. Three things, running hand in hand are responsible for the change and will reshape our world in the very near future.

• The first is the advent of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is the fourth major industrial era since the initial Industrial Revolution of the 18th century. It is characterized by a fusion of technologies that is blurring the lines between the physical, digital, and biological spheres, collectively referred to as cyber-physical systems. It is marked by emerging technology breakthroughs in a number of fields, including robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, quantum computing, biotechnology, the Internet of Things, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), fifth-generation wireless technologies (5G), additive manufacturing/3D printing and fully autonomous vehicles. This is set to change the world and our lives as we know it profoundly and very, very soon. In the next few years it will hit us like a Tsunami, because this explosion of knowledge and technology are exponential.

• The second big milestone is when the brains of human beings, their neocortex, will be linked to machines and the Cloud, making them superhumans, with instant access to all kinds of information, giving them super-intelligence and enhancing their brains with the computational power of hundreds of computers. This will start to happen in the early 2030’s and be in full swing by 2035.

• The third big milestone is the date of 2045 – the so-called Singularity. That is the moment when Artificial Intelligence will surpass human intelligence, when machines will become more intelligent than humans – in an integrated fashion. Today AI’s are already better than humans at diagnosing certain medical conditions, but that same AI cannot analyse legal texts and predict judgments or play chess. That is beginning to change – very soon AI’s will become more and more integrated, to surpass human intelligence by 2045. Some say, “Machine intelligence is the last invention humanity will have to make, because from then on machines will be better than us at inventing.”
All of this will have a profound effect on humanity – from the way we cook, to the way we travel, to the way we procreate, to where live and communicate. It is hard to imagine this future world, because we are used to think incrementally – we think of small adaptations and slow progress from one thing to the next. This is not what is going to happen – in future big changes will come with lightning speed, disrupting existing technology completely. A disruptive technology is one that displaces an established technology and shakes up the industry or a ground-breaking product that creates a completely new industry – e.g. in medicine: instead of examining a patient from the outside, the patient simply swallows a few million nanobots that cruise through his/her system and sends data to an AI that reports on health problems or potential health problems. In future medicine will be preventative rather than treating symptoms – we already have the technology to modify genes that could one day cause diseases. It is being tested on humans as we write.

And disruptive technologies are already changing energy and travel and longevity and law and policing and crowd control and war and food – every part and every segments of human existence.

But what will a future look like when disruptive technologies really take hold, where the human brain is linked (wirelessly) to machines in the cloud (only 12 -15 years away)? And what will happen when machines achieve human levels of intelligence?
We put these questions to three South Africans deeply involved in the future. In fact, they are part of the international think tank called the Singularity University that is aimed at future-proofing the world. Our three guys are on a mission to future-proof Africa, and their vision in profound. And they are well informed! They look forward to a world where poverty has been eradicated by the 2030’s, where energy is free, where humans will live to a few hundred years, where colonies on other planets exist, where there will be no more herds of cattle for meat, where a BUI is the norm and where human will work the minimum and pursue other activities and have the time to ponder the meaning of life.

And they answer the question: are people like Elon Musk who warns against AI not perhaps right in predicting that we can easily become the prey of super intelligent machines? Is a dystopian future not on the cards?

Our three futurists are Mic Mann, Shayne Mann and John Sanei.

In this insert we do a bit of exciting and highly visual time travel, but it is more than mere speculation – everything is based on technologies that are already here and happening, and which can be shown to begin to emerge.

I pre-interviewed the three of them yesterday and they are great speakers. Especially John – he is a renowned international speaker on the future – in high demand and travelling the globe. The Mann brothers has brought the Singularity University to South Africa to help future-proof the continent.

Press Release:


From the Fourth Industrial Revolution to the human brain connecting directly to machines and the Cloud with instant access to information, the world as we know it is evolving at a frantic pace. Future developments which used to seem impossible and many years away, are happening right now. Carte Blanche examines the impact of this new world order.

Script:


V/O:
Imagine waking up in a world where there is no hunger because food is grown in abundance everywhere, even indoors…….. where transport and energy is for free….. where you can send feelings and emotions over the internet … ….… where cell phones have become obsolete….. and where you commute by air.
30
LINK CLAIRE:
This all sounds like science fiction, but it is not. Everything I mentioned will be part of all our lives in the future.
8
V/O:
And do not for one moment think I am talking about a future far away. The future is actually here and is changing our lives as we speak.
11
John Sanei:
I reckon over the next 5 years and 10 years we are going to have a human population that will see more change than we have seen in the previous 200 years.
V/O:
John Sanei is a futurist and international speaker and he says few people realize how fast our world is changing and how much it has already changed.
11
John Sanei:
If you think about it, ij 1998 there were two clear rules. Don’t meet anybody from the internet and don’t get into a stranger’s car. Remember those rules. Today we literally call a stranger from the internet and get into their car. It is called Uber. We literally call a stranger from the internet and go and stay in their home. It is called Air B’nB. We literally call a stranger from the internet and go on a date. It is called Tinder. We are in the future.
V/O:
And it is all around us: there are already robotic companions for the lonely, designer babies are being created, we 3D print homes, and we have flying taxis.
11
John Sanei: British Airways now has a patent pending on a tablet that they want passengers to take in the future that will tell the air hostesses and stewards if you are hungry, drunk, tired, or whatever the base may be.
V/O:
And this phenomenal pace of change has only become possible because of a few critical conditions that are present in today’s world.

Shayne Mann, along with his brother Mic and John Sanei, has a passion to make South Africans and Africans aware that the future has arrived. He says one of these critical conditions that enables fast change today is the availability of global connectivity and ease of communication.
20

Shayne:
During the week I spend as much time talking to people all over the world overseas as I do talking to people in South Africa. That just could not happen in the past, and that is enabling these incredible ideas to flow.
V/O:
The immense computational power of computers that is increasing exponentially is also driving change and makes unheard-of technologies possible.

Today there is also an abundance of capital to fund new technologies than ever before. Incredible amounts of money are invested in new technological advances in medicine, genomics, nanotechnology, robotics, autonomous vehicles and so on.

And the fact that machines and Artificial Intelligence can also learn autonomously, without human intervention is driving massive change.
7



14
LINK CLAIRE:
These conditions combined enable the exponential pace of change we see today, and it also makes it possible for all humans on the planet to benefit from these changes.
V/O:
Futurists talk about the democratization of technology. This means ordinary people now have access to some of the most powerful technologies on earth.
8
Shayne:
If you were the smartest guy in a rural village before, you were trapped, you could not do anything. Now the smartest guy in the most rural village with a hundred-dollar smart phone or a two thousand-rand smart phone, has access to the world’s information.
V/O:
For example, he can take a photo of a growth on somebody’s skin, send it off and have it analysed for skin cancer by an Artificial Intelligence on another continent.
13
LINK CLAIRE:
One of the remarkable technologies that almost all futurists predict is the linking of the human brain to computers or the Cloud.
John Sanei:
Well by 2029 we will all have digital neocortexes into the left side of our brain and this will connect us to become a super human brain connected to all artificial intelligence.
V/O:
Mic Mann says today we ask questions from Google with smart phones. That will change. 5
Mic:. We will be able to ask questions by just thinking.
V/O:
And imagine, that is just 10-11 years away. But the question of course is: would that not mean that our brains and thoughts could be hacked?
10
Mic:
It can be hacked. It can definitely be hacked. Once you have become connected to cloud somebody can hack into your brain and it becomes really dangerous..
V/O:
Such hackers would be able to access your memories and all devices linked to your brain. 5
LINK CLAIRE:
The massive changes that is already reshaping our world will have an enormous impact on the lives of especially poor people.
John Sanei:
We already have less poor people alive than we have ever had. But we must also remember that the future we are moving into moves into something called the zero marginal cost society. Where technology will make the staples and pillars of the economy almost free. The first one we have become comfortable understanding is communication. The likes of Whatsapp has created free communication for most of the world. The next one is energy, and we are going to have access to energy for everybody. The third one will be transportation and access to transportation for everybody. This will then become the beginning of most other things becoming free. If you just think about education, entertainment and these things. If you have access to the internet, you have access to limitless entertainment. And this really unheard of. So the future that we are moving into, one, more people are being uplifted than ever before but also we are moving into a society where everything costs less. So I do think that poverty will be eradicated in the future.

V/O:
Both the Mann brothers and John Sanei are involved in The Singularity University South Africa, which is a think tank offering courses and conferences on how to future-proof South Africa and Africa.
11
Mic:
We are trying to create a community of changemakers across Africa who are able to implement solutions to some of Africa’s and the worlds’s greatest challenges.
LINK CLAIRE:
And in the near future we will experience something called Singularity or The Singularity.
John:
Singularity is a concept that explains when computers will be smarter than human beings. And by 2045 we will have that situation where human beings will not be as smart as computers, and computers would have taken over that intelligence level.
V/O:
Should the Singularity occur, technology will advance beyond our ability to foresee or control its outcomes and the world will be transformed beyond recognition.

Then artificial intelligence will do almost everything, from making pizza to reading the news like this AI news anchor unveiled in China recently. In this scenario, humans will have much more free time.
18
Shayne:
So people are gonna have a lot of time on their hands and the biggest thing is going to be “What is the meaning of life?” You know. What are we here to do? Because most of our day is spent trying to put food on the table for our families. If you don’t have to do that anymore, what are you going to do?
LINK CLAIRE:
But not all futurists are as optimistic and sound a warning note.
V/O:
Instead of a utopian future they see the possibility of a distopian future where things really go wrong, where killer robots pursue humans and where pollution and climate change destroy the entire planet.

And these warnings should be taken seriously as they come from a variety of experts such as Elon Musk and the late Stephen Hawking. However, the vast majority of futurists are positive about the future.
20


John:
I don’t think that we should not focus so much on it not going great. Put some frameworks in place and start focusing and what else we can do to get ourselves to be intergalactic beings, for us to meet other civilizations, for us to educate everybody, how do we give everybody water, how do we make sure everybody has a healthy plate of food on the table. For me that’s the focus, that’s the energy, and that’s the attention we should all give to this sort of technology.
V/O:
And future technologies might hold a few pleasant surprises.
Claire question:
So we talk about all of these grand scale future technologies changing our lives in a major way. But what about everyday mundane tasks and things? Will that also be affected?

Mic
I was recently in SF about two weeks ago and met with this company Endless West. This is their first product called Glyph. It is molecular whiskey.

Claire:
What do you mean molecular whiskey?

Mic:
This whiskey was made in a lab, using different elements. It was made in 12 hours instead of a 12-year process. It was not barrelled or aged. It is whiskey. The only difference it is made with a different process.
Shayne:
So what we do at Singularity University South Africa is we try help organizations understand how close the future is to us now and how they can rather surf the Tsunami of change rather than be engulfed by it. The future is here. The future is here now. Today. The future is here.

This means ordinary people now have access to some of the most powerful technologies on earth. 8 Shayne: If you were the smartest guy in a rural village before, you were trapped, you could not do anything. Now the smartest guy in the most rural village with a hundred-dollar smart phone or a two thousand-rand smart phone, has access to the world’s information. V/O: For example, he can take a photo of a growth on somebody’s skin, send it off and have it analysed for skin cancer by an Artificial Intelligence on another continent. 13 LINK CLAIRE: One of the remarkable technologies that almost all futurists predict is the linking of the human brain to computers or the Cloud. John Sanei: Well by 2029 we will all have digital neocortexes into the left side of our brain and this will connect us to become a super human brain connected to all artificial intelligence. V/O: Mic Mann says today we ask questions from Google with smart phones. That will change. 5 Mic:. We will be able to ask questions by just thinking. V/O: And imagine, that is just 10-11 years away. But the question of course is: would that not mean that our brains and thoughts could be hacked? 10 Mic: It can be hacked. It can definitely be hacked. Once you have become connected to cloud somebody can hack into your brain and it becomes really dangerous.. V/O: Such hackers would be able to access your memories and all devices linked to your brain. 5 LINK CLAIRE: The massive changes that is already reshaping our world will have an enormous impact on the lives of especially poor people. John Sanei: We already have less poor people alive than we have ever had. But we must also remember that the future we are moving into moves into something called the zero marginal cost society. Where technology will make the staples and pillars of the economy almost free. The first one we have become comfortable understanding is communication. The likes of Whatsapp has created free communication for most of the world. The next one is energy, and we are going to have access to energy for everybody. The third one will be transportation and access to transportation for everybody. This will then become the beginning of most other things becoming free. If you just think about education, entertainment and these things. If you have access to the internet, you have access to limitless entertainment. And this really unheard of. So the future that we are moving into, one, more people are being uplifted than ever before but also we are moving into a society where everything costs less. So I do think that poverty will be eradicated in the future. V/O: Both the Mann brothers and John Sanei are involved in The Singularity University South Africa, which is a think tank offering courses and conferences on how to future-proof South Africa and Africa. 11 Mic: We are trying to create a community of changemakers across Africa who are able to implement solutions to some of Africa’s and the worlds’s greatest challenges. LINK CLAIRE: And in the near future we will experience something called Singularity or The Singularity. John: Singularity is a concept that explains when computers will be smarter than human beings. And by 2045 we will have that situation where human beings will not be as smart as computers, and computers would have taken over that intelligence level. V/O: Should the Singularity occur, technology will advance beyond our ability to foresee or control its outcomes and the world will be transformed beyond recognition. Then artificial intelligence will do almost everything, from making pizza to reading the news like this AI news anchor unveiled in China recently. In this scenario, humans will have much more free time. 18 Shayne: So people are gonna have a lot of time on their hands and the biggest thing is going to be “What is the meaning of life?” You know. What are we here to do? Because most of our day is spent trying to put food on the table for our families. If you don’t have to do that anymore, what are you going to do? LINK CLAIRE: But not all futurists are as optimistic and sound a warning note. V/O: Instead of a utopian future they see the possibility of a distopian future where things really go wrong, where killer robots pursue humans and where pollution and climate change destroy the entire planet. And these warnings should be taken seriously as they come from a variety of experts such as Elon Musk and the late Stephen Hawking. However, the vast majority of futurists are positive about the future. 20 John: I don’t think that we should not focus so much on it not going great. Put some frameworks in place and start focusing and what else we can do to get ourselves to be intergalactic beings, for us to meet other civilizations, for us to educate everybody, how do we give everybody water, how do we make sure everybody has a healthy plate of food on the table. For me that’s the focus, that’s the energy, and that’s the attention we should all give to this sort of technology. V/O: And future technologies might hold a few pleasant surprises. Claire question: So we talk about all of these grand scale future technologies changing our lives in a major way. But what about everyday mundane tasks and things? Will that also be affected? Mic I was recently in SF about two weeks ago and met with this company Endless West. This is their first product called Glyph. It is molecular whiskey. Claire: What do you mean molecular whiskey? Mic: This whiskey was made in a lab, using different elements. It was made in 12 hours instead of a 12-year process. It was not barrelled or aged. It is whiskey. The only difference it is made with a different process. Shayne: So what we do at Singularity University South Africa is we try help organizations understand how close the future is to us now and how they can rather surf the Tsunami of change rather than be engulfed by it. The future is here. The future is here now. Today. The future is here.

metadata.Further information: In the past, we thought of the future as, well… the future. We thought of a time, still years away. But that has changed. In the latter half of the 20th century more knowledge was created than in the previous 10 000 years of human existence. In the first 10 years of the 21st Century more knowledge was created that in all of the 20th Century, and it is speeding up exponentially. And this will, and is, changing our lives and our world profoundly. Three things, running hand in hand are responsible for the change and will reshape our world in the very near future. • The first is the advent of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is the fourth major industrial era since the initial Industrial Revolution of the 18th century. It is characterized by a fusion of technologies that is blurring the lines between the physical, digital, and biological spheres, collectively referred to as cyber-physical systems. It is marked by emerging technology breakthroughs in a number of fields, including robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, quantum computing, biotechnology, the Internet of Things, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), fifth-generation wireless technologies (5G), additive manufacturing/3D printing and fully autonomous vehicles. This is set to change the world and our lives as we know it profoundly and very, very soon. In the next few years it will hit us like a Tsunami, because this explosion of knowledge and technology are exponential. • The second big milestone is when the brains of human beings, their neocortex, will be linked to machines and the Cloud, making them superhumans, with instant access to all kinds of information, giving them super-intelligence and enhancing their brains with the computational power of hundreds of computers. This will start to happen in the early 2030’s and be in full swing by 2035. • The third big milestone is the date of 2045 – the so-called Singularity. That is the moment when Artificial Intelligence will surpass human intelligence, when machines will become more intelligent than humans – in an integrated fashion. Today AI’s are already better than humans at diagnosing certain medical conditions, but that same AI cannot analyse legal texts and predict judgments or play chess. That is beginning to change – very soon AI’s will become more and more integrated, to surpass human intelligence by 2045. Some say, “Machine intelligence is the last invention humanity will have to make, because from then on machines will be better than us at inventing.” All of this will have a profound effect on humanity – from the way we cook, to the way we travel, to the way we procreate, to where live and communicate. It is hard to imagine this future world, because we are used to think incrementally – we think of small adaptations and slow progress from one thing to the next. This is not what is going to happen – in future big changes will come with lightning speed, disrupting existing technology completely. A disruptive technology is one that displaces an established technology and shakes up the industry or a ground-breaking product that creates a completely new industry – e.g. in medicine: instead of examining a patient from the outside, the patient simply swallows a few million nanobots that cruise through his/her system and sends data to an AI that reports on health problems or potential health problems. In future medicine will be preventative rather than treating symptoms – we already have the technology to modify genes that could one day cause diseases. It is being tested on humans as we write. And disruptive technologies are already changing energy and travel and longevity and law and policing and crowd control and war and food – every part and every segments of human existence. But what will a future look like when disruptive technologies really take hold, where the human brain is linked (wirelessly) to machines in the cloud (only 12 -15 years away)? And what will happen when machines achieve human levels of intelligence? We put these questions to three South Africans deeply involved in the future. In fact, they are part of the international think tank called the Singularity University that is aimed at future-proofing the world. Our three guys are on a mission to future-proof Africa, and their vision in profound. And they are well informed! They look forward to a world where poverty has been eradicated by the 2030’s, where energy is free, where humans will live to a few hundred years, where colonies on other planets exist, where there will be no more herds of cattle for meat, where a BUI is the norm and where human will work the minimum and pursue other activities and have the time to ponder the meaning of life. And they answer the question: are people like Elon Musk who warns against AI not perhaps right in predicting that we can easily become the prey of super intelligent machines? Is a dystopian future not on the cards? Our three futurists are Mic Mann, Shayne Mann and John Sanei. In this insert we do a bit of exciting and highly visual time travel, but it is more than mere speculation – everything is based on technologies that are already here and happening, and which can be shown to begin to emerge. I pre-interviewed the three of them yesterday and they are great speakers. Especially John – he is a renowned international speaker on the future – in high demand and travelling the globe. The Mann brothers has brought the Singularity University to South Africa to help future-proof the continent.
